state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's review the concept of even numbers. Remember, an even number can be represented as 2n, where n is an integer. In the expression you provided, we have 2n + (2m + 1). Can you identify the even number in this expression based on what we just discussed?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, so 2n is the even number because it's got the 2 in front? But then what about the (2m + 1) bit - is that even or odd? I'm confused because I thought the whole thing 2n + (2m + 1) was supposed to show that two odd numbers add up to even, but now I'm not sure which parts are which.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with identifying 2n as the even number. In the expression 2n + (2m + 1), the term (2m + 1) represents an odd number because it has an odd integer (1) added to an even number (2m). Can you now see how the sum of an even number and an odd number results in an even number?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher addresses the misconception about 2n representing even numbers but makes a critical mathematical error in Turn 3 by claiming 2n + (2m+1) shows that an even plus odd equals even, when the problem actually requires showing two odd numbers sum to even, and the student remains confused about which parts represent odd numbers.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses questioning to guide discovery rather than directly explaining with worked examples, which is inconsistent with the traditional strategy of explicit instruction and demonstration.
